summary.headline: Euro Pratik Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19.8% YoY to INR115.7 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.4% and PAT at INR26.2 crores.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR115.7 crores, up 19.8% YoY from INR96.6 crores, with EBITDA of INR37.4 crores (31.4% margin) and PAT of INR26.2 crores (22% margin). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR219 crores (up 35.9%), with EBITDA of INR66.5 crores and PAT of INR46.2 crores. Management attributed margin pressure to crude, freight and raw material costs, and said the acquired entities run at lower margins, diluting the consolidated figure. The company signed a deal on 5 November 2026 to acquire 51% of Drashti Surfaces Private Limited for up to INR31.12 crores plus a loan commitment of up to INR20 crores, with closing expected by 30 November 2026.

financial_highlights.change: vs 32.5% in Q2 FY26 per analyst question

Core business EBITDA margin / net profit margin

segments.name: Decorative wall panels (core)
segments.commentary: Contributed 65.5% of Q2 FY27 revenue per analyst. Management guided 50% to 55% of revenue over the long term, with wall panels sourced from more than 45 contract manufacturers.

segments.name: Laminates
segments.commentary: Contributed 24% of Q2 FY27 revenue per analyst. Drashti adds paper laminates and veneers, which management expects to become a significant revenue contributor.

segments.name: Core business (Euro Pratik and Glorio)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 gross margin 44.8%, EBITDA margin 36%, net profit margin 26.5%, excluding acquired entities. Margins described as steady at EBITDA and PAT level.

segments.name: Acquired entities (URO Veneer World, Chawla Brothers, Drashti)
segments.commentary: Run at lower margins, about 18% to 19% EBITDA margin per management, which dilutes consolidated margin. Drashti is project-led and supplies top builders in Mumbai.

guidance_outlook: Targeted revenue growth of at least 25% to 30% CAGR over the next 3 years.
Blended EBITDA margin expected to hold around 37% and PAT margin at 25% to 26%, per management's answer on blended economics.
Drashti acquisition: long-stop date 90 days from 5 November 2026; closing expected by 30 November 2026.
Target return on capital employed of 18% to 20% from acquisitions.
Working capital expected to remain around 150 days, plus or minus 10%, excluding the URO Veneer World consolidation distortion.
Management said the product mix is expected to stay broadly constant, with wall panels at 50% to 55% of revenue.
risks_watch: Drashti closing by 30 November 2026 (long-stop 90 days from 5 November 2026) and integration progress.
Cash and cash equivalents fell to INR8.4 crores in September 2026 from INR16.4 crores in March 2026, while borrowings rose.
EBITDA margin fell to 31.4% from 32.5% YoY, with input-cost pressure from crude, freight and raw materials.
Dependence on about 45 contract manufacturers, many overseas, and exposure to geopolitical and freight disruption.
Working capital days remain at about 150 days, and the company has not provided a clear reduction plan.
summary.management_tone: Confident and growth-focused on acquisitions and revenue momentum, with management calling Q2 the highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and profit. Cautious on margins, attributing pressure to crude, freight and raw material costs and to the lower-margin acquired entities. Several answers on wall panel manufacturing and margin uplift were hedged, with decisions left to future evaluation.
key_quotes: Despite these external headwinds, Euro Pratik has maintained its growth momentum, demonstrating the resilience of our business and the strength of our operating model, resulting in highest ever revenue, quarterly EBITDA and profit in the history of the company.
So company has always remained and tried to remain a net debt-free company, and comfortable cash positions was always there.
So, our intention is to grow at least 25% to 30% CAGR in the next 3 years.
Drashti does not make wall panels and this transaction is about veneers and laminates.

qa_highlights.question: Why have working capital days risen sharply over recent years, and what structural changes are being made?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Alpesh Sangoi said the rise was distorted by URO Veneer World, integrated from 1 December 2025, where the 31 March 2026 balance sheet was consolidated while only four months of P&L were included. Excluding this, working capital stays around 150 days, plus or minus 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What drives future acquisitions: geography, product portfolio or forward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Pratik Singhvi said the aim is building manufacturing backup in India, which the company lacked, given factors beyond its control. Drashti is the third acquisition, mainly to make products in India for the domestic market, after two earlier forward-integration deals.

qa_highlights.question: How much would Drashti add at peak capacity and how would it affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Sangoi said peak capacity could generate about INR180 crores of turnover. Drashti's EBITDA margin is currently 16% to 17%, and margins should expand as utilisation rises and fixed costs are absorbed. Blended EBITDA is guided around 37% and PAT at 25% to 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the acquisition let Euro Pratik manufacture wall panels in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Sangoi said Drashti does not make wall panels and the deal covers veneers and laminates. It lays groundwork for a future wall panel base on the 180,000 sq ft surplus FSI, to be evaluated in stages.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth target and what caused the 31.4% EBITDA margin versus 32.5% a year earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Sangoi said the target is at least 25% to 30% CAGR over the next 3 years. He said the core business margins held steady at EBITDA and PAT level, while lower-margin acquired entities and higher crude, logistics and input costs diluted the consolidated margin.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company reduce dependence on distributors and sell directly to end customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Pratik Singhvi said the digital platform generates many end-customer inquiries and Drashti's project business supplies top Mumbai builders, creating a direct-project opportunity. Majority of sales still go through distributors, and URO Veneer World's retail outlet stake gives direct end-user feedback.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company's cash position and balance sheet being managed after the acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Sangoi said acquisitions were funded from internal accruals, with about INR110 crores of cash outflow for URO Veneer World and Chawla Brothers. Net cash surplus from operations is about INR7.5 crores per month, and the company aims to remain net debt-free.

capex_capacity: Drashti laminates plant at 70% to 75% capacity utilisation; veneer plant at 45% to 50%.
Drashti's peak-level capacity, converted to value, could generate about INR180 crores of turnover.
Bhilad factory has surplus FSI of about 180,000 square feet for further expansion, and Drashti has surplus land to build a wall panel facility.
Management said any wall panel manufacturing project would be evaluated in stages after integrating veneers and laminates, subject to technology, capital cost and cost-benefit analysis.
Drashti deal: 51% gross stake for up to INR31.12 crores plus loan commitment up to INR20 crores; long-stop date 90 days from 5 November 2026, closing expected by 30 November 2026.
demand_pricing: Management said Q2 FY27 was the highest-ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA and profit, despite crude, freight and raw material headwinds.
Distribution spans 195 Indian cities through 208 distributors; portfolio covers 30+ categories and more than 3,850 SKUs across wall panels, premium laminates, interior films and structural profiles.
Management said about 75% of core business sales come from products launched within the previous 12 to 14 months.
Wall panel share guided at 50% to 55% of revenue long term, with laminates and other categories making up the rest; management said the mix would stay broadly constant.
Market share in organised decorative wall panels cited at 15.87%, based on FY2024 financials; management said share has risen since.
Core business (Euro Pratik and Glorio) margins described as steady at EBITDA and PAT level, with acquired entities at lower margins diluting the consolidated figure.
Acquired entities EBITDA margin cited at 18% to 19%; Drashti's current EBITDA margin cited at 16% to 17%.
Management guided blended EBITDA margin around 37% and PAT margin 25% to 26%.
Management said most products are made outside India, so crude and logistics costs rose.

adds.what: Drashti Surfaces surplus land for a future wall panel facility (not yet approved; staged evaluation)

growth.why: Management targets at least 25% to 30% revenue CAGR over three years and cites 75% of core sales from products launched in the last 12-14 months, plus the Drashti acquisition (closing by 30 Nov 2026) adding laminates and veneers; no hard capacity additions are committed beyond Drashti's existing plant and possible staged wall panel expansion.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides blended EBITDA margin around 37% vs 31.4% in Q2 FY27, but core margin is steady at 36% and the gap relies on Drashti (16-17% margin) scaling up with utilisation; crude and freight costs are a headwind.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Drashti closing by 30 Nov 2026 adds laminates and veneers capacity, with peak capacity worth about INR180 crores of turnover versus current utilisation of 70-75% (laminates) and 45-50% (veneers); no new plant is committed beyond that.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets at least 25-30% revenue CAGR over 3 years, H1 FY27 revenue grew 35.9% YoY to INR219 crores, and about 75% of core sales come from products launched in the last 12-14 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Surplus FSI of about 180,000 sq ft at Bhilad and surplus land at Drashti could host a wall panel facility, but management said it will be evaluated in stages subject to technology, capital cost and cost-benefit, with no approval yet.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided a steady 37% blended EBITDA margin and 25-26% PAT margin, and Q2 margin already fell YoY to 31.4% from 32.5%, so no clear upside to guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin pressure from crude, freight and raw materials, lower-margin acquired entities at 18-19% EBITDA, and Drashti's 16-17% margin could push consolidated margins below the 37% guide if the acquisitions do not ramp.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said about 75% of core sales come from products launched in the last 12-14 months, and Drashti adds paper laminates and veneers that management expects to become a significant contributor.

rows.label: Drashti project business with top Mumbai builders
rows.why: Drashti supplies top Mumbai builders on a project basis, and management sees a direct-project opportunity, but no order numbers were given.

rows.label: Net debt-free aim amid rising borrowings
rows.why: Cash fell to INR8.4 crores in Sep 2026 from INR16.4 crores in Mar 2026 while borrowings rose, but operations generate about INR7.5 crores per month and management aims to stay net debt-free.

rows.label: Working capital days around 150
rows.why: Working capital stays at about 150 days (plus or minus 10%) and management gave no clear reduction plan, so a near-term improvement is not signalled.

tone.note: Management was confident on revenue momentum, the Q2 record and the 25-30% CAGR target, but cautious on margins, blaming crude, freight and lower-margin acquisitions; analysts probed margin dilution, working capital days and wall panel manufacturing plans.
